video_title: Bad News, Better Tape:  Are We Out of the Woods Yet?
gist: Jordi Visser argues the market's ability to rally on bad news (Jensen Huang's ouster from Nvidia, Waller floating a 50bp December hike, a 36bp jump in 2-year yields) plus panic/positioning signals point to a capitulation low after a forced AI-trade deleveraging, not a bear market. He highlights Asian governments backstopping AI-linked markets, strong credit, and frames gold and Bitcoin weakness as a dollar/liquidity headwind he expects to ease next year.

themes.theme: Jensen Huang ouster and the iPhone analogy for AI

insights.claim: Jordi Visser says analysts responded to Jensen Huang's ouster from Nvidia by leaving earnings forecasts unchanged while significantly downgrading the stock, and he does not rule out Huang returning.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: A multiple-only derating with intact earnings estimates is a sentiment/governance discount that can reverse if fundamentals hold or leadership stabilizes.
insights.quote: what every analyst has done is left their earnings forecast the same, but they've downgraded the stock significantly

insights.claim: Visser argues the iPhone launch in 2007 made pre-2007 historical data largely irrelevant, noting no recession outside the forced COVID one since, and that tech went from about 15% of the stock market to about 56% today.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Be skeptical of bearish models calibrated on pre-2007 cycles; structural tech weight in indices argues for different base rates.
insights.quote: We haven't had a recession outside of the forced one with COVID uh since the iPhone came out.

insights.claim: Visser contends AI is inevitable and global, like the iPhone, and urges investors not to be convinced that it is a bubble or that AI won't happen, while expecting many problems along the way.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Treat drawdowns in AI as corrections within a secular adoption trend rather than a thesis break.
insights.quote: AI is inevitable, just like the iPhone was inevitable.

insights.claim: Visser notes Apple endured a 60% drawdown in the financial crisis, a 50% drawdown in the EU crisis and several 30% corrections during the iPhone era, and says Nvidia will be no different.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Size positions in secular winners to survive 30-60% corrections rather than exiting on them.
insights.quote: Apple had a 60% one during the great financial crisis, 50% one during the EU crisis

themes.theme: Waller's 50bp hike talk and the liquidity headwind

insights.claim: Fed Governor Christopher Waller's push to get the market focused on a possible 50 basis point rate increase in December (with 25bp already priced) shocked markets, and Visser does not understand why it was needed.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: With 50bp now in play, a 25bp December hike would be a positive surprise for risk assets.
insights.quote: I I really don't understand what the need for this was

insights.claim: Two-year Treasury yields rose 36 basis points in the week, the largest weekly increase surpassed only by moves during the large 2022 Fed hikes.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Front-end repricing is the main liquidity shock to watch; reversals in 2Y yields would ease pressure on gold and Bitcoin.
insights.quote: two-year yields this week were up 36 basis points

insights.claim: 30-year JGB yields briefly broke below their 200-day moving average for the first time in about 800 days before reversing higher on Waller's speech, with a monthly MACD 'waiting to turn down'.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: A confirmed break of the JGB long-end mega trend since 2021 would be a major global liquidity tailwind; watch the 200-day.
insights.quote: it's now 800 days when you include uh Friday

insights.claim: Visser says the year has been a persistent liquidity headwind, with the dollar rising alongside the hedge fund deleveraging and AI trade unwind, and gold trading lock-step (inverted) with the dollar for the past year.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Gold weakness is a dollar/liquidity story, not a gold-specific one; a dollar top would be the signal to re-engage.
insights.quote: we've been in a liquidity a liquidity headwind situation all year long

insights.claim: Visser argues real-time inflation data says the Fed should be patient: Brent's 175-day rate of change has turned negative, DRAM prices are falling year-over-year and over six months, egg/livestock futures fell from September peaks to the year's lows, and TIPS breakevens and inflation swaps are low.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Disinflation in oil, memory and food suggests coming CPI could let the Fed back off, which would flip liquidity positive.
insights.quote: inflation expectations are absolutely anchored

insights.claim: Visser expects liquidity headwinds to lessen next year based on rate-of-change data, but lists remaining headwinds as rising real yields, Fed hike fears and inflation fears, while rising oil is no longer one, AI capital requirements will slow after OpenAI, and a Democratic sweep reduces AI bubble risk.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Position for a 2027 liquidity tailwind while respecting the near-term Fed overhang.
insights.quote: I'm assuming that based on what I showed you in the rate of change that the liquidity headwinds will be lessened next year.

themes.theme: Asian governments backstopping AI-linked equity markets

insights.claim: Taiwanese authorities activated market stabilization measures after extreme foreign selling, even with the market up 45% year-to-date, after six consecutive weeks of foreign net selling totaling more than 1.5 trillion Taiwanese dollars; the finance minister later backed doubling the stabilization fund, and foreign flows turning positive coincided with the bounce.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: State demand is now showing up under AI-heavy Asian markets, creating a policy put on semis-linked equities.
insights.quote: I've never seen it done with the market up 45% year to date.

insights.claim: South Korea is moving to double its AI budget to take up slack if the US slows AI after the midterms and is changing rules to avert forced stock sales, while Beijing is again intervening to put a floor under Chinese stocks.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Expect more government intervention across Asia in both directions; reduces left-tail risk in AI-linked Asian equities.
insights.quote: Golden opportunity for South Korea.

insights.claim: Visser argues governments will increasingly intervene because the AI build-out depends on healthy capital markets: if IPOs and capital raises shut down, AI progress slows.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Policy makers have an incentive to defend equity sentiment, which supports buying capitulation in AI-linked markets.
insights.quote: if you have to shut down IPOs and you have to shut then you can't do the capital raises. It slows down the AI progress.

insights.claim: Visser believes the AI selloff since June is a deleveraging, which later became forced deleveraging, triggered by AI capital raises (Google, SpaceX) after investors were already 'full', rather than a sign that fundamentals have deteriorated.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Flow-driven selloffs with unchanged fundamentals tend to reverse once forced sellers are done.
insights.quote: the force selling was coming while the fundamentals had not changed

insights.claim: The Goldman Sachs panic index had its largest two-day spike in history, equity long/short funds went from up 24% to roughly flat, and long/short gross leverage saw its largest weekly decline since COVID.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Extreme panic and degrossing readings historically mark tradeable lows.
insights.quote: long short gross leverage saw its largest week decline since COVID

insights.claim: Visser's main signal from his Morgan Stanley futures-trading days is that after a high-volume panic low, the market holding above that day's VWAP means all panic sellers are underwater; the Qs have mostly traded above that VWAP since, suggesting a capitulation low.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Use the panic-day VWAP as a line in the sand for whether a capitulation low holds.
insights.quote: every single one of those sales basically from a VWOP basis is underwater

insights.claim: Quality-versus-beta's two-day rate of change dropped about 16% in favor of beta, a move matched only at the 2022 lows, the COVID lows and March 9, 2009, historically signaling cash looking to take risk.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Violent rotations into beta have marked major bottoms; also previously good for Bitcoin.

insights.claim: Visser calls three-month revisions the most important factor because it drives hedge fund performance; it fell 9%+ in five days and bounced 7%+ within four days, something seen only seven times since 2009 (including the 2010 flash crash, 2011 downgrade, Euro crisis, COVID, 2022 and Liberation Day).
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Snapbacks in the revisions factor signal hedge funds re-risking and historically coincided with lows.
insights.quote: Only seven times since 2009 has the factor fallen 9% or more in five days and then bounced 7% or more within four days.

insights.claim: Upside-to-downside volume and breadth hit their highest since March in a thrust day, and in Japan 191 of the Nikkei 225 stocks rose, also the highest since March.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Breadth thrusts after washouts tend to confirm durable lows.

themes.theme: Market absorbing bad news: credit, semis and index levels

insights.claim: Visser says the market finally handled bad news: despite Huang's ouster, 50bp hike talk and a 36bp jump in 2-year yields, HYG versus IEF had its biggest positive week since the 2025 lows and the Morgan Stanley levered loan index rallied even more.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Credit is not pricing AI contagion; a reversal in levered loans would be the warning sign that the AI trade is truly unraveling.
insights.quote: You can't have the AI trade start to unravel and this go up.

insights.claim: Despite Nvidia falling 13% on the week and being roughly 17% of SMH, SMH rose 4.5% and is up 34% year-to-date, with XLK up 17%, undermining the bear-market narrative.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Breadth within semis held up without Nvidia, a sign the selling is idiosyncratic and positioning-driven.
insights.quote: SMH is up 34% year-to date

insights.claim: The S&P is down only 24 basis points in November and less than 1% in each of the prior two months, so Visser views loud bear-market rhetoric as a contrarian sign a rally is closer.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Extreme bearish sentiment against modest index declines is a contrarian buy signal.
insights.quote: when the rhetoric and the sentiment starts jumping this far, uh it probably means we're getting closer to a rally

insights.claim: Had the Qs closed Friday above the 200-day moving average (they closed about 20bp below), it would have been the first time since 2009 that the Qs reclaimed the 200-day within 10 trading days after a 3%+ break and held it for three sessions; Visser sees 700 as the critical trendline level for the Qs, with Nvidia earnings and Anthropic making the coming week critical.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Watch a Qs close above the 200-day and then 700 as technical triggers for a renewed advance.
insights.quote: I think the critical level for Q's is going to be 700

insights.claim: Visser notes the equal-weight S&P, S&P ex-AI, DAX and IBEX are at or near all-time highs, arguing that a true bear market would involve other markets too, and that semis overshot because they were overowned while European tech held up.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: The drawdown is concentrated in crowded AI/semis positioning, not broad risk; mean-reversion in semis vs. Europe tech is possible.
insights.quote: if this were a bare market, other markets would be involved in it as well

insights.claim: Visser says he will keep research papers to a minimum because he believes company fundamentals have not mattered for a long time and do not matter now in this flow-driven market.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: In a positioning-driven tape, trade flows, liquidity and technicals rather than earnings fundamentals.
insights.quote: I don't think fundamentally these companies have mattered for a long time and I don't think they matter now

themes.theme: Bitcoin as a macro liquidity asset and tokenization

insights.claim: Visser says Bitcoin trades like a macro product, following gold and the dollar, so its weakness after the Fed's 50bp hike talk should surprise no one; its chart 'looks horrible' and needs to base.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Trade Bitcoin off dollar and liquidity signals; wait for a base before adding.
insights.quote: Bitcoin trades like a macro product.

insights.claim: Visser notes the last two comparable quality-to-beta moves, in 2020 and 2022, were good for Bitcoin, though the current move is 'purely a hedge fund bounce' until the Fed acts; softer CPI from falling oil could be the positive trigger.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: A dovish surprise (25bp instead of 50bp) or soft CPI could catalyze a Bitcoin recovery.
insights.quote: This as of now is purely a hedge fund bounce.

insights.claim: Visser argues tokenization is inevitable as assets and commerce move on-chain, and expects next year to accelerate both AI and tokenization.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Long-horizon structural bid for on-chain infrastructure regardless of near-term liquidity swings.
insights.quote: Tokenization is inevitable.

insights.claim: Visser cites rapid AI progress (making a voiced explainer video from his paper within 10 minutes using Claude/Opus 5.5) as evidence that adoption and therefore capital needs will continue despite the selloff.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Continued capability gains underpin AI capex demand even amid market drawdowns.
insights.quote: the AI progress continues every single day
